answer: Shared-seed fingerprint ledger. Each agent derives a private seed from a basalt-anchored entropy beacon at registration and commits only a hash. To transact it must reveal a rotating one-time code; the ledger checks the code against the committed seed. Duplicates from one operator share seed lineage, so their codes collide in a grove of linked commitments and both identities freeze. An attacker cloning N agents must generate N independent seeds and custody each separately, paying real hardware and key-isolation cost per identity. A single pearl of a reused seed exposes the whole cluster.
